verdicts.quote: A ticket is waiting on its requester while its status is `resolved`
a ticket resolved at T0 whose status is still `resolved` at T0 + REMINDER_AFTER_HOURS (default 72h)
further ticks after the reminder, even once it is sent, enqueue nothing more.
A ticket is waiting on its requester while its status is `resolved`
verdicts.missing: Status determines whether an agent edit, reopening or closure ends the wait. A builder still needs to know how a requester reply is recognized and translated into a transition out of resolved.

verdicts.quote: `to` is the ticket's requester, `ticket` is its id, and the rendered message has subject `[<id>] Waiting on you` and a body naming the ticket title and saying it can be reopened by replying.
verdicts.missing: Whether the body includes the elapsed wait and how delivery handles a requester value that is not an email address.

verdicts.quote: a body naming the ticket title and saying it can be reopened by replying.
verdicts.missing: Both notices direct the requester to reply. The reminder's wording leaves open whether the resolved notice's seven-day deadline still applies, including when the reminder arrives after that deadline.

verdicts.quote: the check is a job of the worker; no timer of its own and no request does it.
at most one event per (ticket, resolve time) key, before and after restart
verdicts.missing: The key prevents a second event. The spec leaves duplicate delivery of the same event unresolved if a send succeeds and the worker retries before recording success.

verdicts.quote: a ticket that is open, in_progress or closed is never reminded, however old.
verdicts.missing: Whether the worker verifies the current status and resolve period at enqueue time if the ticket changes after the scan.

verdicts.quote: delivery follows the outbox rules unchanged (retry with backoff, dead after 5).
verdicts.missing: One event per resolved period rules out a replacement for a dead event. The spec leaves open whether enqueueing requires a registered reminder template.

verdicts.quote: the job scans all tickets each tick
verdicts.missing: The scan includes existing tickets and their resolve times are available from history. The spec does not explicitly decide whether the first tick enqueues the entire pre-deployment backlog.

verdicts.quote: a ticket reopened (resolved to open) and resolved again starts a new period: reminded again 72h after the new resolve, not before.
at T0 + 71h59m no reminder; at exactly T0 + 72h a reminder (threshold is inclusive).
verdicts.missing: The production clock and time zone for comparison, and whether nights, weekends or holidays delay a due reminder.

verdicts.quote: no new stored ticket field; the reminder lives in the outbox and persists with it. Invariant: at most one event per (ticket, resolve time) key, before and after restart
a test that loads a data file with no reminder events.
verdicts.missing: Old files can represent zero reminders without a new ticket field. The loader's behavior for malformed reminder event data, including whether it rejects the file and names the offending field, is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: A reminder is not a ticket change: no audit entry, `updated` unchanged.
no UI, no new input or endpoint
verdicts.missing: Who may change the deployment setting and whether anyone may manually send or suppress an individual reminder through existing administrative tools.

verdicts.quote:
an unusable value (`abc`, `0`, `-1`) stops start with a message naming `REMINDER_AFTER_HOURS`. Confirmed by a config test.
- Boundary: `WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=0` turns reminders off with the rest of the background work.
a notifier test reading the NOTIFY_FILE line.
verdicts.missing: The file provides a record of delivery. The spec does not identify where operators see upcoming reminders or specify how reporting preserves raw CLI column positions.

verdicts.quote: the job scans all tickets each tick; at current size acceptable, no numeric bound invented.
verdicts.missing: The next tick bounds enqueueing in worker ticks. There is no maximum delivery delay, per-tick enqueue limit or requirement that scanning thousands of tickets leave delivery responsive.

verdicts.quote: Created and resolved notifications, the lifecycle table, API responses, the audit log, the data file format (version 1; old files load) and the existing 117 tests are unchanged.
verdicts.missing: Preservation of list-filter behavior and of CLI and weekly report output is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: CHANGELOG section and version bump (1.5.0), README config row, docs/operations.md note, ADR 0009 for the reminder design
verdicts.missing: An update to the API documentation is unspecified.
